newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close lower on minister's remarks.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close lower on minister's remarks.

text.p: Stocks closed lower on Saturday in weak trading dampened by the finance minister's remarks that he was not considering any artificial steps to boost the economy, brokers said.
"The minister's comment depressed the market," said Kim Choon-kwon of Daewoo Securities.
The composite index closed 6.15 points lower at 675.07.
"Market fundamentals will remain weak next week, with the index testing 650," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik told reporters he would not adopt boosting measures but focus on stabilising the economy and reducing the current account deficit.
Volume totalled 23.84 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 37.38 million on Friday.
Losers outpaced gainers 561 to 224, with 124 unchanged.
The minister also said on Saturday he expected gross domestic product to grow five to six percent this year against an estimated 6.9 percent rise in 1996.
Brokers said customer deposits with brokerage firms were estimated at 2.8 trillion won, down from a year high of 3.05 trillion in mid-February.
